resources.string: Enter a valid ISO date from 1900-01-01 to 2100-12-31.
Enter a whole number from −10,000 to 10,000, without separators or a plus sign.
Select days to exclude every week. None is allowed; at least one weekday must remain working.
At least one weekday must remain working.

Optional: up to 100 dates separated by commas or new lines (maximum 1,200 characters). Duplicate dates count once; dates already excluded by weekday are not subtracted twice. Do not add empty entries.
Use valid ISO dates in the supported range, with at most 100 entries and 1,200 characters.

The start date is not counted. An offset of zero returns the start unchanged, even on a non-working day. Negative offsets walk backward. Counts include the end date only if it is a working day; earlier end dates give a negative count, or zero when no working dates are traversed. Swapping endpoints can change the magnitude because a different endpoint is excluded.

Calendar dates only: no time zones, regional holidays or official holiday calendar are inferred. Enter any holidays you want excluded. This is a planning calculation, not a guarantee about business opening days.
Explicit imports and saved setups restore inputs only; press Calculate. Remember results can restore a completed calculation when reopening.
Enter your dates and working-day rules, then calculate.
The result would leave the supported date range. Reduce the offset or change the start date.
The saved setup is invalid. Your current inputs were kept.
Keep both dates and the offset valid when switching calculations. Add/subtract uses the start and offset; count uses the start and end.
